packages.title: ONS transport-industry 78 MtCO2e residence emissions QA
facts: ONS estimates the transport and storage industry emitted about 78 MtCO2e on a residence basis in 2024.
The transport industry is defined using SIC-based economic-industry classification.
Residence-basis transport includes activity by UK resident units beyond UK borders where applicable.
The figure is distinct from domestic-transport territorial emissions.
No parcel allocation is supported.

packages.title: ONS transport-industry 16.3 percent residence share QA
facts: ONS reports transport and storage as 16.3% of total residence-basis GHG emissions in 2024.
This is an industry share within environmental accounts.
It should not be mixed with DfT domestic-transport territorial shares.
The denominator is total residence-basis emissions.
No parcel percentage is inferred.

packages.title: ONS air transport 51.6 percent of transport-industry emissions QA
facts: ONS reports air transport accounted for 51.6% of transport-industry residence emissions in 2024.
The denominator is transport-industry emissions, not total UK emissions.
Air-transport industry accounting differs from territorial domestic aviation treatment.
The statistic is an economic-industry allocation.
It is not a property-level emissions measure.

packages.title: ONS 2024 GHG intensity 140 tonnes per £1m GVA QA
facts: ONS reports UK GHG emissions intensity at about 140 tonnes CO2e per £1 million GVA in 2024.
The metric relates emissions to economic output.
Intensity is neither total emissions nor physical energy consumption.
The denominator must be preserved when comparing values.
No parcel intensity is created.

packages.title: ONS GHG intensity 72 percent decline since 1990 QA
facts: ONS reports UK GHG emissions intensity fell 72% between 1990 and 2024.
The cited intensity changed from about 500 to 140 tonnes CO2e per £1 million GVA.
The trend is based on residence environmental accounts and economic output.
A falling intensity does not necessarily imply the same percentage fall in absolute emissions.
No local parcel trend is inferred.

packages.title: ONS fossil fuels 77.7 percent direct energy share QA
facts: ONS reports fossil fuels accounted for 77.7% of UK direct energy consumption in the latest environmental accounts context.
Direct energy use is an energy measure rather than a GHG total.
Fuel shares require the stated environmental-accounts boundary.
Energy consumption and emissions must not be treated interchangeably.
No parcel fuel share is inferred.

packages.title: ONS renewable energy 15.3 percent direct energy share QA
facts: ONS reports renewable energy increased to 15.3% of direct energy consumption in the environmental accounts context.
This is a direct-energy share rather than an electricity-generation share.
The denominator differs from Energy Trends generation statistics.
Renewable energy use does not itself report avoided emissions.
No parcel allocation is made.

packages.title: ONS territorial residence footprint three-basis QA
facts: ONS identifies three principal UK GHG measures: territorial, residence and footprint.
Territorial emissions cover emissions occurring within UK borders.
Residence emissions align with UK resident economic units and National Accounts.
Footprint emissions allocate global supply-chain emissions to UK final demand.
The three measures are not interchangeable.

packages.title: Territorial versus residence GHG boundary QA
facts: Territorial and residence emissions use different geographic and economic boundaries.
Territorial accounting supports national climate-target reporting.
Residence accounting supports economic-industry analysis.
Differences can arise from international transport and resident-unit activity abroad.
Neither basis identifies a parcel without separate geometry and activity evidence.

packages.title: Footprint consumption-emissions boundary QA
facts: Footprint emissions are consumption-based and include supply-chain emissions associated with UK final demand.
Footprint accounting differs from emissions physically occurring inside the UK.
Imports can contribute to UK consumption-footprint emissions.
Footprint estimates are modelled economic-environmental accounts rather than direct site measurements.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: Local-GHG 71 percent of authorities decreased QA
facts: DESNZ reports GHG emissions decreased between 2023 and 2024 in 71% of UK local authority areas.
The release identifies 255 of 361 local authority areas with decreases.
These are local-authority estimates using nationally consistent methods.
A local-authority trend does not imply every parcel within the area changed similarly.
No parcel trend is inferred.

packages.title: Local-GHG energy end-use allocation QA
facts: DESNZ local GHG statistics distribute energy-supply emissions based on where energy end use occurs.
This differs from a pure source-location allocation for power generation.
The method improves local comparability but remains an allocation model.
Local authority totals therefore require methodology context.
No parcel end-use value is inferred without direct binding.

packages.title: Local-GHG waste-arising allocation QA
facts: DESNZ distributes waste emissions in local statistics based on where waste arises.
The allocation is not necessarily the physical location of landfill or treatment facilities.
Waste activity and waste GHG emissions are separate measures.
Local-authority waste emissions are modelled allocations.
No parcel treatment-site value is inferred.

packages.title: Local-GHG aviation shipping military exclusion QA
facts: DESNZ states local GHG statistics exclude aviation, shipping and military transport emissions from local allocation where there is no obvious basis for allocation.
Those emissions remain relevant to national inventories but are not assigned to local authorities in this dataset.
Local totals therefore do not equal all national emissions divided geographically.
Exclusions must be preserved in comparisons.
No parcel value is inferred from omitted categories.

packages.title: Local-GHG fluorinated-gas local allocation exclusion QA
facts: DESNZ states fluorinated gases are not included in local estimates where suitable data are unavailable for local allocation.
National inventory coverage and local allocation coverage differ.
A missing local category must not be treated as zero emissions.
Data absence is distinct from a measured zero.
No parcel fluorinated-gas value is inferred.

packages.title: Local-GHG population and employment proxy QA
facts: DESNZ notes smaller emission sources are often mapped using proxy information such as population or employment.
Proxy allocation is modelled evidence rather than direct source measurement.
Proxy uncertainty increases caution for small-area interpretation.
Local estimates are nationally consistent but not cadastral measurements.
No parcel value is generated from a population or employment proxy.

packages.title: Local-authority allocated GHG 2 percent fall 2024 QA
facts: DESNZ reports total GHG emissions allocated to UK local authorities fell about 2% from 2023 to 2024.
The local-authority aggregate uses the local allocation methodology.
The decrease is consistent with the national direction but the accounting boundaries differ.
Local changes vary substantially by area and sector.
No uniform parcel reduction is assumed.

packages.title: Local-GHG electricity-supply decline drivers QA
facts: DESNZ links much of the 2024 local-authority emissions decrease to lower electricity-supply emissions.
The release cites higher net electricity imports, greater renewable generation and closure of the UK's last coal-fired power station as drivers.
System-level drivers are not site measurements.
Electricity-supply changes affect end-use allocated local totals through methodology.
No parcel electricity emissions are inferred.
